tasks.title: Action layer scaffold: TaskAction enum and ActionError
acceptance: `src/ui/actions/mod.rs` defines a `TaskAction` enum with exactly one variant per in-scope action: `Add`, `Edit`, `Complete`, `Uncomplete`, `Delete`, `Move`, `Reorder`, `AddComment`, each carrying its own payload struct (content/description/project/section/parent/due string/priority/labels for `Add`; changed-field options for `Edit`)
`Edit` payload uses `Option<T>` per field so an unchanged field is distinguishable from a field cleared to empty; a unit test asserts `None` vs `Some("")` round-trip distinctly

`src/error.rs` gains `ActionError` (thiserror, `#[non_exhaustive]`) with at least `NotAuthenticated`, `Queue { source }`, `Cache { source }`, `InvalidInput { field: &'static str, reason: String }`, and `AppError` gains `Action(#[from] ActionError)` rendered with an `action: ` prefix, matching the existing `Api(..)` / `Auth(..)` style
A unit test formats every `ActionError` variant with `{}` and `{:?}` and asserts the fixture token `tok_fake_abc123` never appears
`src/ui/actions/mod.rs` is wired into the `ui` module tree with module docs; no HTTP, no SQL and no ratatui widgets in this task
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Pure type/scaffold task so the rest of the epic can land in parallel. Follow the error conventions already set by `ApiError`/`AuthError` in `src/error.rs` (thiserror, `#[non_exhaustive]`, crate-wide `Result<T> = Result<T, AppError>`). The `src/ui/` module tree and its `mod ui;` declaration come from the TUI shell epic (EPIC-07), which is being built in parallel - if `src/ui/mod.rs` does not exist yet on your base branch, stop and ask rather than inventing the shell. Never touch the `Secret`/`REDACTED` helper in `src/log.rs`.

tasks.title: Map TaskAction to Sync API write commands
acceptance: A pure function turns a `TaskAction` into the Sync command(s) to enqueue, using the existing command/envelope types from `src/api/sync.rs`
Command `type` strings are exactly `item_add`, `item_update`, `item_complete`, `item_uncomplete`, `item_delete`, `item_move`, `item_reorder`, `note_add`; a unit test asserts the mapping per action
Every produced command carries a freshly generated v4 `uuid`; two calls for the same action produce different uuids (unit-tested)
`Add` (task) and `AddComment` on a not-yet-synced parent produce a `temp_id`; non-create actions produce no `temp_id` (unit-tested)

`item_move` serialises exactly one destination key (`project_id` xor `section_id` xor `parent_id`); supplying zero or more than one destination returns `ActionError::InvalidInput` instead of building a command
`item_reorder` serialises an `items` array of `{id, child_order}` pairs in ascending `child_order` with no gaps (unit-tested on a 5-item list)
`Edit` serialises only the fields actually changed - a test with only `priority` set asserts the args map has exactly one key
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Reuse the wire types and `RESOURCE_TYPES`-style single-source-of-truth pattern from `src/api/sync.rs` (EPIC-03) rather than hand-rolling JSON. This task builds commands only - it does not enqueue or touch the DB (that is T-703). Serde args are a `HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>` as the sync envelope already expects.

tasks.title: Action dispatcher: atomic enqueue plus optimistic cache apply
acceptance: `dispatch(action)` writes the queued command(s) and the optimistic cache mutation inside a single SQLite transaction via the EPIC-05 enqueue API; a unit test that forces a rollback asserts neither a queued command nor a mutated row remains

Optimistic apply covers every action: add inserts an item row with the temp id, edit updates fields, complete/uncomplete flip `checked`, delete removes (or tombstones) the row, move rewrites the destination key, reorder rewrites `child_order`, comment inserts a note row
Dispatch never performs network I/O and returns without waiting for a sync; a unit test asserts no API client is invoked
Dispatch returns the ids/uuids it produced so the caller can correlate later per-command failures
When no token is configured, dispatch returns `ActionError::NotAuthenticated` and enqueues nothing
Unit tests run against an in-memory SQLite store with fixture data (no real account data, no real ids)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: This is the single seam every UI action goes through, so keep it UI-free (no ratatui types) and testable headlessly. Reuse the EPIC-05 enqueue + optimistic-apply API and the EPIC-04 store rather than opening your own connection; `temp_id_mapping` resolution is owned by EPIC-05 and must not be reimplemented here. Follow the existing in-memory-store test pattern used by the cache tests.

tasks.title: Add-task form widget
acceptance: A `TaskForm` widget renders fields for content, description, project, section, parent, due string, priority and labels, with one focused field at a time

Tab/Shift-Tab cycle focus, Esc cancels, Enter on the last field (or a bound submit key) emits a submit event carrying the typed values; a snapshot test of the rendered buffer covers empty and filled states
Submitting with empty content is refused in-widget with an inline message and emits no submit event (unit-tested)
The widget is state-only: it returns an `Add` payload and performs no enqueue, no DB and no network calls
Renders correctly at the 80x24 minimum terminal size (snapshot test); longer content wraps rather than panicking on narrow widths
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Follow the widget + snapshot-test conventions established by the TUI shell epic (EPIC-07) - reuse its theme/style helpers and its buffer-snapshot test helper instead of adding a new snapshot library. Quick-add natural-language parsing is explicitly out of scope (decision D1, lands in EPIC-11).

tasks.title: Wire add-task form to dispatch and refresh the list
acceptance: A bound key (default `a`) opens the add-task form prefilled with the currently selected view's project/section, and `A` opens it as a sub-task of the selected task

Submitting the form calls `dispatch(TaskAction::Add(..))` exactly once and the new task appears in the rendered list on the next frame, before any sync - a test with the API mock paused asserts the row is visible
Cancelling with Esc enqueues nothing and leaves the cache unchanged (asserted on the queue and item tables)
The new bindings are registered in the keymap source of truth so the `?` help overlay lists them without manual edits (asserted by a test that reads the keymap)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: The keymap registry and help overlay are owned by EPIC-07; add entries through its registration API so the overlay stays drift-free - do not hardcode key strings in the overlay. If the shell's keymap file lives at a different path on your base branch, stop and ask before touching extra files.

tasks.title: Edit task fields from the detail pane
acceptance: A bound key (default `e`) opens the task form prefilled from the selected task; the form is reused from T-704 rather than duplicated
Submitting dispatches exactly one `TaskAction::Edit` whose payload contains only the fields the user changed (test: change priority only -> payload has one `Some` field)
Submitting with no changes dispatches nothing
Quick inline edits for priority (`p` then 1-4) and due string (`d` then text) dispatch an `Edit` without opening the full form
Edited values are visible in the list and detail pane on the next frame with the API mock paused
New bindings are registered in the keymap so the help overlay lists them (asserted by test)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Reuse `TaskForm` in an 'edit' mode; the `Option`-per-field `Edit` payload from T-701 is what keeps 'unchanged' and 'cleared' distinct. Due strings are passed through verbatim to the server (`due.string`); no local natural-language parsing.

tasks.title: Complete, uncomplete and delete with confirmation dialog
acceptance: Default binding `x` (or Space) dispatches `Complete` on an open task and `Uncomplete` on a completed one; exactly one command is enqueued per press

Default binding `D` opens a reusable confirm dialog naming the task; confirming dispatches exactly one `Delete`, declining or Esc enqueues nothing and mutates nothing (both asserted on the queue and item tables)
The confirm dialog widget is generic (title, message, confirm/cancel) and snapshot-tested at 80x24
Completing a task removes it from the active list on the next frame with the API mock paused; uncompleting restores it
Completing a recurring task follows the documented behaviour and a doc-comment links to the EPIC-08 docs note (see T-714)
New bindings are registered in the keymap so the help overlay lists them (asserted by test)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Recurring-task completion while offline is open question 6 in the requirement - implement the simplest behaviour (enqueue `item_complete`, let the server compute the next occurrence, do not fabricate a next due date locally) and document it; do not invent a local recurrence engine.

tasks.title: Move task between project, section and parent
acceptance: Default binding `m` opens a filterable picker listing projects, their sections and (for sub-task moves) candidate parents, read from the cache
Choosing a destination dispatches exactly one `Move` command carrying exactly one destination key; a test asserts the serialised args contain one of `project_id`/`section_id`/`parent_id`
Moving a task under itself or its own descendant is refused with an inline message and enqueues nothing (unit-tested on a 3-level fixture tree)
The task disappears from the source list and appears under the destination on the next frame with the API mock paused
The picker widget is snapshot-tested with an empty filter and a filter matching one entry
New bindings are registered in the keymap so the help overlay lists them (asserted by test)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Read destinations through the EPIC-04 cache queries (projects/sections by project, items by parent); do not query the API. Creating new projects/sections from the picker belongs to EPIC-09 and is out of scope here.

tasks.title: Reorder tasks within a list
acceptance: Default bindings `K`/`J` move the selected task up/down within its sibling group; selection follows the moved task
Each move dispatches exactly one `Reorder` command whose `items` array covers every sibling whose `child_order` changed, with contiguous ascending orders (unit-tested on a 5-item sibling list)
Moving the first item up or the last item down is a no-op: nothing is enqueued and nothing is mutated
Reordering never crosses section or parent boundaries (a test asserts siblings of a different parent keep their `child_order`)
Cached `child_order` is updated optimistically so the new order survives a re-read of the list from the cache within the same session
New bindings are registered in the keymap so the help overlay lists them (asserted by test)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: `child_order` semantics come from EPIC-03 domain types and the EPIC-04 ordering queries; reuse the existing ordered-read query rather than sorting ad hoc in the UI. Cross-list drag (move + reorder in one gesture) is out of scope - move is T-708.

tasks.title: Comments: view pane and add-comment form
acceptance: Default binding `c` opens a comments view for the selected task listing cached notes oldest-first with author and timestamp, scrollable with `j/k`

A bound key inside the view opens a text input; submitting dispatches exactly one `AddComment` (`note_add`) command with a `temp_id` and the comment appears in the list on the next frame with the API mock paused
Submitting an empty comment is refused and enqueues nothing
Comments on a still-temp-id task reference the task's temp id so EPIC-05 `temp_id_mapping` can rewrite it (asserted on the enqueued args)
Comment view is snapshot-tested with zero, one and many comments at 80x24
New bindings are registered in the keymap so the help overlay lists them (asserted by test)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Text-only comments; attachments and reactions are explicitly out of scope. Notes are already modelled in `src/api/model/note.rs` and cached by EPIC-04 - read them through the cache.

tasks.title: Surface per-command failures in status bar and errors view
acceptance: Failed queue commands (EPIC-05 `failed` state) drive a status-bar indicator showing the failure count alongside the existing sync state
A bound key (default `E`) opens an errors view listing each failed command with its action name, affected task content and the verbatim server error text
A transient toast appears for the most recent failure and disappears after a bounded time or on keypress (unit-tested with an injected clock, not real sleep)
Dismissing an entry in the errors view clears it from the queue's failed set; a test asserts the row is gone after dismissal

Local state after a failure follows the keep/rollback rule defined by EPIC-05 - the UI never decides it itself; a test with one keep-class and one rollback-class error asserts the rendered list matches the store
No error text rendered in the UI or logged contains token material (test asserts the fixture token `tok_fake_abc123` never appears)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: The status bar itself is owned by the TUI shell epic (EPIC-07) and is fed by EPIC-06 sync-state events - extend its state struct with a failure count through the shell's existing event channel instead of rendering a second status line. Log server error text through the `Secret`-aware logging in `src/log.rs`.

tasks.title: Integration tests: one correct command per action, offline and temp_id cases
acceptance: For each of add / edit / complete / uncomplete / delete / move / reorder / comment, a test drives the action headlessly and asserts the mock API receives exactly one command of the expected type with a fresh `uuid`; creates carry a `temp_id`
A test with the mock API paused asserts the UI buffer reflects every action before any request is sent
Delete: declining the confirmation leaves the queue and item tables untouched; confirming enqueues exactly one `item_delete`
Offline test: mock API down, all eight actions performed, then mock restored - every change lands exactly once and the set of `uuid`s seen server-side has no duplicates
Temp-id test: create a project (EPIC-09 path or direct queue seed) then a task in it, submit one batch, and assert the cached task's `project_id` is the real id and no temp id remains in the DB
Failure test: mock returns an error `sync_status` for one command - the error text appears in the rendered errors view and local state matches the EPIC-05 keep/rollback rule
Tests use fixture data only (no real ids, tokens, or account data) and run offline in CI
`cargo test --all` passes
tasks.context: Follow the existing integration-test style in `tests/` (EPIC-02's `tests/auth_cli.rs` and the EPIC-03 API tests) - mock HTTP server, temp dirs, no real network. Drive the TUI through the shell's headless test harness (EPIC-07) with a fixed-size test backend rather than spawning a real terminal.

tasks.title: E2E: reorder and edits persist across sync and restart
acceptance: Scenario: launch the app against a seeded cache and mock API, reorder three tasks, complete one, edit one, let a sync cycle run, quit, relaunch - the rendered list order and task states match what was left behind
A second sync after restart sends no duplicate commands (mock asserts each `uuid` seen exactly once across both runs)
Edits made while the mock is offline survive a restart and flush after the mock returns
The terminal is restored cleanly on quit in every scenario (test asserts the alternate screen is exited)
Test is deterministic (injected clock, no real sleeps > 50ms) and uses fixture data only
`cargo test --all` passes
tasks.context: Restart means tearing down and recreating the app over the same state dir, not spawning a subprocess, unless the shell epic already provides a binary-level harness. Reuse the fixtures from T-712 rather than duplicating them.

tasks.title: Document task-action keybindings and offline/recurring behaviour
acceptance: Documents every default binding added by this epic (add, sub-task add, edit, quick priority/due, complete/uncomplete, delete+confirm, move, reorder, comments, errors view) and notes they are rebindable from `config.toml`
Explains the optimistic-write model: action -> queued command + immediate local apply, flushed by the background sync, and what the status bar shows while pending or offline
States the decided behaviour for completing a recurring task while offline (open question 6) and its visible consequence for the user
Describes what happens when the server rejects a command: where the error appears and whether local state is kept or rolled back
Lists a short manual check sequence a human can run against a test account (no real credentials or ids in the doc)
Follows the structure of the existing `docs/manual/epic-02-auth-checks.md` and `docs/manual/epic-03-sync-api.md`
tasks.context: Docs only - no code changes. The recurring-offline note is a hard acceptance item of the epic ('behaviour must be documented in the help/docs whichever way it is decided'), so it must match what T-707 actually implements.
